title: Autopilot
summary: Autopilot runs the Waves of one Epic one after another, with no person at the Orchestrator. Press Autopilot on the Epic frame: the run sends the ready Wave, waits until it is over, then sends the next one. The same run also starts from /worfy:epic-wave typed in a Session's chat, or from asking the agent in words once you confirm worfy's dialog.

It stops when no Wave is ready, when you press Stop autopilot, or when something goes wrong. While it runs, no one answers the Orchestrator, so its questions are refused, and each step goes to a journal. No run starts by itself.

scene.description: One run of Autopilot. On the Canvas, the Epic frame holds its Tickets and the Ready wave chip; the Orchestrator and the implementers it starts stand below. Outside the Canvas, Autopilot takes the ready Wave and sends Run wave to the Orchestrator. The Orchestrator starts implementers in the background, and they work on the Tickets and set their status. When the turn has ended, Autopilot judges the Wave and takes the next one. Autopilot waits for the Limits to reset and records the run in a journal.

labels.epicNote: the Autopilot button is on its frame
labels.waveNote: the Tickets that can be taken in parallel now
labels.step1: The Autopilot button on the Epic frame starts a run. The run takes the ready Wave: the Tickets of the Epic that can be taken in parallel now.
labels.step2: It sends the Project's Run wave text, which names those Tickets, to the Orchestrator. During the run the Orchestrator is unattended: its permission requests and questions are refused.
labels.step3: The Orchestrator runs the Wave, usually by starting implementers in the background. The agents set the status of the Tickets themselves: worfy writes none.
labels.step4: The Wave is over when its turn has ended, nothing runs in the background and no Ticket of the Wave is in work. Then the run sends the next ready Wave, or stops when there is none.
labels.step5: When the Limits refuse a turn, the run waits for the reset plus 2 minutes and goes on. Each Wave, wait and stop goes to the run's journal.

flow.description: The data flow of a run. The Autopilot button calls autopilot.start over IPC, and the run checks the start. The run gives the cycle its state and one event and gets back the next state and effects. The send-wave effect goes to the launcher, which sends the Run wave text to the Orchestrator's Session. The Session's events and the changes the workflow watch sees come back to the run. The run writes the journal, one JSON line per step, keeps the display on, and sends each new state back over IPC as autopilot.changed.

labels.step1: The button calls autopilot.start. The checks go in order: no run in the Project, the self-project refusal and the template, the workflow and the Epic, then the origin key and the Linked machines.
labels.step2: setUnattended starts the Orchestrator again unattended, continuing its SDK session. The run opens its journal, keeps the display on and opens a workflow watch.
labels.step3: Each event goes to the cycle, and its effects go to the journal or the Session. send-wave reaches the launcher, which reads the workflow once: the text names the Wave's Tickets.
labels.step4: The Session's events and the workflow's changes come back as cycle events. Each new state goes to every window as autopilot.changed.

text: The cycle is a pure function: the state of a run and one event in, the next state and a list of effects out. Its phases are starting, sending, turn, tasks, settling and stopped. Every step of a run goes through one queue, so events are handled in order.
Every Wave after the first usually goes to a new SDK session of the Orchestrator, so its context does not grow.

/worfy:epic-wave typed with an Epic, a Wave or Tickets and without attachments does not reach the agent: agent.send hands it to ChatStarts.startFromChat, as the Canvas MCP tool autopilot_start does after its dialog. A run over named Tickets takes only those into its Waves and stops with tickets-done once they are done.

limits: One run per Project at a time. The same Epic of the same repository running on a Linked machine refuses the start; Start anyway is the only way past.
A development build refuses a run on worfy's own repository, its worktrees included.
A Ticket of the Wave still in work after the turn: the run waits up to 10 minutes, then stops with wave-unfinished. Background tasks with no event for an hour: background-stalled.
A refusal by the Limits: the run waits until the reset plus 2 minutes, or tries every 30 minutes when no reset time is known; past 24 hours it stops with limits-timeout.
In the Run mode Start window, a Wave that usually takes longer than the whole window stops the run at once with window-too-short.
The dialog of autopilot_start waits 10 minutes; an unattended Session gets a refusal with no dialog.
